common.metadataTitle: RoCourse — Learn Luau & Roblox for Free
common.metadataDescription: A free, interactive course for learning Luau and Roblox game development from absolute zero — through hands-on lessons, real game code, and a complete final project. No paywall, no sign-up.

activity.buildTycoonDescription: Click a coin to earn, buy upgrades that multiply every click, and climb an idle fortune. Pure UI-to-server economy.

activity.hintMissingLocal: Add the `local` keyword at the start — without it, this becomes a global variable.
activity.hintMissingEquals: You're missing the `= value` — a declaration assigns a value to the name.
activity.hintNameMismatch: The variable name doesn't match what the rest of the script expects — check the name.
activity.hintMissingValue: A declaration needs `= <value>` after the name — you're missing the value.
activity.hintExtraParts: Your line has extra parts after the value — keep it to the single corrected line.
activity.hintNumberNotString: The value should be a number, not a string — remove the quotes.
activity.hintStringNotNumber: The value should be a string — wrap it in quotes.
activity.hintStringMismatch: The string value isn't what the script expects — check the text.
activity.hintNumberMismatch: The value on the right side of `=` is wrong — double-check the number.
activity.hintRhsMismatch: The value after `=` isn't what the script expects — check what's being assigned.
activity.hintMissingToken: You're missing `{token}` — compare your line to the pattern shown in the lesson.
activity.hintIncomplete: Your line looks incomplete — compare it to the pattern shown in the lesson.
activity.hintMissingValueGeneric: You're missing a value — check what should be assigned.
activity.hintExtraTokens: Your line has extra parts — keep it to the single corrected line.
activity.hintCompare: Compare your line to the pattern shown in the lesson — what's different?

reference.pageIntro: A searchable cheat sheet of Luau syntax and common patterns. Each card links to the lesson that teaches the idea in full.
reference.entries.hello-world.title: Hello, world
reference.entries.hello-world.description: The classic first program. Every Luau script can call print.
reference.entries.comments.title: Comments
reference.entries.comments.description: Comments are notes for you (and future-you) — Luau ignores them.
reference.entries.statements.title: Statements
reference.entries.statements.description: Semicolons are optional. One statement per line is the usual style.
reference.entries.local-variables.title: Local variables
reference.entries.local-variables.description: Declare values with local. Locals stay inside the block they live in.
reference.entries.reassigning.title: Reassigning variables
reference.entries.reassigning.description: Variables hold one value at a time — you can change what they hold.
reference.entries.main-types.title: The main types
reference.entries.main-types.description: Numbers, strings, booleans, and nil are the core building blocks.
reference.entries.type-checking.title: Check a value's type
reference.entries.type-checking.description: type() returns the name of a value's type as a string.
reference.entries.multiple-assignment.title: Multiple assignment
reference.entries.multiple-assignment.description: Assign several variables at once, and use it to swap values.
reference.entries.string-basics.title: String basics
reference.entries.string-basics.description: Text in Luau is a string. Double or single quotes both work.
reference.entries.concatenation.title: Concatenation
reference.entries.interpolation.title: String interpolation
reference.entries.interpolation.description: Backticks let you embed values directly inside a string.
reference.entries.string-methods.title: Common string helpers
reference.entries.string-methods.description: The string library covers the day-to-day text operations.
reference.entries.arithmetic.title: Arithmetic
reference.entries.arithmetic.description: The usual math, plus floor division and remainder.
reference.entries.comparison.title: Comparison
reference.entries.comparison.description: Compare values for equality and ordering. ~= means "not equal".
reference.entries.boolean-logic.title: Boolean logic
reference.entries.boolean-logic.description: and, or, and not combine true/false conditions.
reference.entries.compound-assignment.title: Compound assignment
reference.entries.compound-assignment.description: Shorthand for updating a variable with an operation.
reference.entries.if-else.title: if / elseif / else
reference.entries.if-else.description: Run different code depending on a condition.
reference.entries.while-loop.title: while loop
reference.entries.while-loop.description: Repeat while a condition stays true.
reference.entries.numeric-for.title: Numeric for loop
reference.entries.numeric-for.description: Count up (or down) over a range. A third number sets the step.
reference.entries.break.title: break
reference.entries.break.description: Exit a loop early from inside it.
reference.entries.define-call.title: Define & call
reference.entries.define-call.description: Bundle code into a named function, then call it with arguments.
reference.entries.return-values.title: Return values
reference.entries.return-values.description: A function can hand a value back to whoever called it.
reference.entries.multiple-returns.title: Multiple returns
reference.entries.multiple-returns.description: Return several values at once and capture them all.
reference.entries.anonymous-functions.title: Anonymous functions
reference.entries.anonymous-functions.description: Functions are values too — pass them around as callbacks.
reference.entries.varargs.title: Varargs
reference.entries.varargs.description: ... accepts any number of extra arguments.
reference.entries.create-index.title: Create & index
reference.entries.create-index.description: Tables hold multiple values. Lists start at index 1; dictionaries use keys.
reference.entries.dictionary-iteration.title: Iterate a dictionary
reference.entries.dictionary-iteration.description: pairs() visits every key and value.
reference.entries.list-iteration.title: Iterate a list
reference.entries.list-iteration.description: ipairs() walks a list in order, 1 to #list.
reference.entries.table-methods.title: Table helpers
reference.entries.table-methods.description: table.insert and table.remove keep lists tidy.
reference.entries.task-wait.title: task.wait
reference.entries.task-wait.description: Pause the current script for a number of seconds.
reference.entries.task-spawn.title: task.spawn
reference.entries.task-spawn.description: Run a function without blocking the code after it.
reference.entries.warn.title: warn
reference.entries.warn.description: Print a message that stands out in the Output window.
reference.entries.common-mistakes.title: Common mistakes
reference.entries.common-mistakes.description: The two errors beginners hit most: = instead of == and a missing end.

quiz.introCount: {bank} questions in the bank — each quiz draws {size} random ones.

quiz.introRuleTwo: See the right answer instantly, with a quick explanation.

quiz.questions.q1.question: What does the print function do in Luau?
quiz.questions.q1.options.2: Outputs text to the Output window
quiz.questions.q1.explanation: print() writes text to Studio's Output window — your first debugging tool.
quiz.questions.q2.question: How do you write a single-line comment in Luau?
quiz.questions.q2.explanation: Luau uses -- for comments. // is C-style and is not valid Luau.
quiz.questions.q3.question: Which keyword creates a new local variable?
quiz.questions.q4.question: What does the # operator return when applied to a string?
quiz.questions.q4.explanation: #"hello" returns 5 — the length of the string in bytes.
quiz.questions.q5.question: What is the value of "10" + 5 in Luau?
quiz.questions.q5.explanation: Luau automatically coerces numeric strings in arithmetic, so "10" + 5 is 15.
quiz.questions.q6.question: What does the % operator do?
quiz.questions.q6.options.1: Returns the remainder of a division
quiz.questions.q6.explanation: The modulo operator gives the remainder, e.g. 7 % 3 is 1.
quiz.questions.q7.question: Which operator joins two strings together?
quiz.questions.q8.question: What is the result of 5 ^ 2?
quiz.questions.q9.question: After local x = 10 and then x = x + 5, what is x?
quiz.questions.q10.question: What does type(true) return?
quiz.questions.q10.explanation: type() returns a string describing the value's type.
quiz.questions.q11.question: Which values are 'truthy' in Luau?
quiz.questions.q11.explanation: Only false and nil are falsy — even 0 and empty strings are truthy.
quiz.questions.q12.question: What does nil represent in Luau?
quiz.questions.q13.question: What is the difference between = and ==?
quiz.questions.q14.question: What is the result of true and false?
quiz.questions.q15.question: What is the result of not false?
quiz.questions.q16.question: Which values make if x then run its block?
quiz.questions.q17.question: When does if health <= 0 then run?
quiz.questions.q17.options.0: When health is zero or negative
quiz.questions.q18.question: What is the purpose of elseif?
quiz.questions.q18.options.0: Check another condition when the previous was false
quiz.questions.q19.question: How does every if statement end in Luau?
quiz.questions.q20.question: What does local x = false and error("boom") evaluate to?
quiz.questions.q20.explanation: and short-circuits: when the left side is falsy, the right side is never evaluated.
quiz.questions.q21.question: How many times does the body of for i = 1, 5 do run?
quiz.questions.q22.question: What values does for i = 1, 5, 2 do produce?
quiz.questions.q22.explanation: A step of 2 skips every other value, ending at 5.
quiz.questions.q23.question: A while true do loop with no exit condition will…
quiz.questions.q24.question: In repeat ... until condition, when is the condition checked?
quiz.questions.q24.options.1: After the body runs (at least once)
quiz.questions.q25.question: What does break do inside a loop?
quiz.questions.q26.question: What skips the rest of the current iteration in a Luau loop?
quiz.questions.q26.explanation: Luau supports continue to jump to the next iteration.
quiz.questions.q27.question: How do you define a function named heal?
quiz.questions.q28.question: What keyword sends a value back out of a function?
quiz.questions.q29.question: A function that never hits return returns…
quiz.questions.q30.question: In local function add(a, b) what are a and b?
quiz.questions.q31.question: What does ... mean in a function like local function log(...)?
quiz.questions.q31.options.0: It accepts any number of extra arguments
quiz.questions.q31.explanation: The variadic ... lets a function accept extra arguments.
quiz.questions.q32.question: Calling part:SetPosition() instead of part.SetPosition(part) — what does the : do?
quiz.questions.q32.options.1: Passes part as the first argument (self)
quiz.questions.q32.explanation: The colon passes the instance itself as the first argument, known as self.
quiz.questions.q33.question: In Luau, what is the index of the first element of an array?
quiz.questions.q34.question: What is #{10, 20, 30}?
quiz.questions.q34.explanation: # returns the length of an array-like table.
quiz.questions.q35.question: If t = {name = "Ada"}, how else can you write t.name?
quiz.questions.q36.question: What does table.insert(t, x) do?
quiz.questions.q36.options.1: Appends x to the end of t
quiz.questions.q37.question: What is the result of ("hello"):sub(1, 2)?
quiz.questions.q38.question: What does string.upper("hi") return?
quiz.questions.q39.question: What does table.concat({"a", "b"}, "-") return?
quiz.questions.q40.question: What is the result of 5 // 2 in Luau?
quiz.questions.q40.explanation: // is floor division — it rounds down, so 5 // 2 is 2.
quiz.questions.q41.question: What does math.random(1, 6) return?
quiz.questions.q42.question: What does math.floor(3.7) return?
quiz.questions.q43.question: What does tonumber("42") return?
quiz.questions.q44.question: Where are the parts in a game's world stored?
quiz.questions.q45.question: Which service tracks the players in your game?
quiz.questions.q46.question: Where does a LocalScript run?
quiz.questions.q47.question: How do you get a player's character model?
quiz.questions.q48.question: What does Instance.new("Part") do?
quiz.questions.q49.question: Which event fires when one part touches another?
quiz.questions.q50.question: What does CFrame.new(0, 10, 0) describe?
quiz.questions.q50.explanation: A CFrame stores both a position and a rotation in 3D space.

dailyChallenge.title: Daily challenge
dailyChallenge.introBody: One challenge, once a day — a quick question or a broken script to debug. Beat it to keep your streak alive.
dailyChallenge.introRuleOne: A fresh challenge every day, same for everyone.
dailyChallenge.introRuleTwo: Some days it's a question, some days it's a script to fix.
dailyChallenge.introRuleThree: Beating it feeds your streak even without a lesson.
dailyChallenge.doneBodyWrong: The answer was {letter} — come back tomorrow.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-nil-part.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-nil-part.options.0: The script is missing a local variable
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-nil-part.options.1: SpawnPart doesn't exist, so part is nil
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-nil-part.options.3: print needs a string, not a number
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-nil-part.explanation: workspace.SpawnPart is nil when no part named SpawnPart exists — you can't read .Position off nil. Use WaitForChild("SpawnPart") or check with FindFirstChild first.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-arithmetic-nil.question: What's the bug?
Can't add to nil — coins has no starting value
The variable name has a typo
local must come after the assignment
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-arithmetic-nil.explanat: coins was declared without a value, so it's nil, and nil + 10 is an error. Give it a real start: local coins = 0.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-call-nil.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-call-nil.options.1: Functions must be called with a colon
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-call-nil.options.2: makeCoins isn't defined yet — it's nil
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-call-nil.options.3: The script is missing a require
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-call-nil.explanation: You can't call nil. Define the function before calling it — and double-check the spelling. Scripts run top to bottom.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-undefined-global.option: coin doesn't exist — you meant coins
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-undefined-global.explan: coin (no s) was never declared. Studio warns "Undefined global" — variable names must match exactly.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-missing-end.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-missing-end.options.0: Missing end to close the if block
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-missing-end.options.2: print can't be called inside an if
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-missing-end.explanation: Every if needs a matching end. Studio reports "Expected end" and points at the line where the block opened.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-string-concat.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-string-concat.explanati: + is for arithmetic. To join strings in Luau use ..: print("Hello " .. name).
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-zero-index.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-zero-index.options.0: items[0] is nil — Luau arrays start at 1
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-zero-index.explanation: Luau arrays are 1-indexed. items[1] is "sword" and items[0] is nil.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-localplayer.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-localplayer.options.0: LocalPlayer only exists on the client — it's nil on the server
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-localplayer.options.3: You need to require the Players service
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-localplayer.explanation: The server has no single "LocalPlayer" — it sees all players. On the server, use game.Players.PlayerAdded instead.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-character-nil.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-character-nil.options.0: Character doesn't exist yet — it spawns after joining
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-character-nil.options.2: PlayerAdded only fires on the client
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-character-nil.options.3: The character needs to be cloned manually
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-character-nil.explanati: A player's Character is nil until it loads. Wait for CharacterAdded, then WaitForChild("Humanoid").
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-infinite-loop.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-infinite-loop.options.0: The loop never ends, so print never runs
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-infinite-loop.options.2: while loops need an end keyword
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-infinite-loop.explanati: while true do with no exit condition and no task.wait() runs forever — the script never reaches print and Studio may freeze.
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-touch-event.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-touch-event.options.0: Touch isn't a property — the event is called Touched and needs :Connect
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-touch-event.options.1: Doors can't be touched in code
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-touch-event.explanation: Events aren't assigned — they're connected with :Connect, and the touch event is called Touched: door.Touched:Connect(function() ... end).
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-property-typo.question: What's the bug?
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-property-typo.options.0: Positon isn't a property — it's Position
dailyChallenge.challenges.debug-property-typo.explanati: Studio reports "Positon is not a valid member". Tiny typos in property names are a classic first bug — and why autocomplete helps.
